requirement:
> `Close a delivered search and record dependencies for snippets you used to
> justify your conclusion without an additional source read. search_id is the
> result's UUID and used is an array of its short entry tags, e.g.
> {"search_id":"11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111","used":["1"]}. Entries
> whose source you also read may be omitted; including them is harmless. Use
> used:[] when no entries qualify, including an empty search. Every delivered
> search must be finished before submission. The result is {search_id,
> finished:true}; no additional source is delivered.`
rationale: The requirement `requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.mcp.description` fixes the text of the `finish_search` tool description. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#impl[Session<'_,%20D>/ToolSession<D>]/fn[definitions]` builds the `FINISH_SEARCH` definition with a `description` string. I compared that string with the requirement text and they are word for word identical. That includes the example JSON, the `used:[]` guidance, the finish-before-submission sentence, and the final sentence about the `{search_id, finished:true}` result. The same definition's parameters declare `search_id` as a UUID string and `used` as an array of strings, both required. This matches the description. `fn[definitions]` carries the `{impl}` reference to the requirement, and the definition is built there, so no other root needs a reference. The `finish_search` search-obligation tests in the same file's `tests` module (`search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot`) carry `{test}` references to `finish_search.mcp`, but not to this description requirement. The task asked for a structural assessment, so I did not treat that as a gap. I found no `{fixme}` acknowledgments, and I found no structural gap.
